title: Ellora Caves
summary: The Ellora caves, cut into a basalt cliff near Aurangabad in Maharashtra, form a run of 34 Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monasteries and temples made from about the 6th to the 10th century or later. They include the Kailasa temple (Cave 16), the largest single monolithic excavation according to the ASI, attributed by it to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO dates the monuments from 600 to 1000 CE; the ASI says the caves are datable from about the 6th-7th to the 11th-12th century. Start follows UNESCO, with a century of margin earlier for the ASI wording. End is the present (the site survives).

as_recorded.value: datable from circa 6th – 7th century A.D. to 11th – 12th century A.D.

when.display: c. 600–1000 CE (ASI: 6th/7th to 11th/12th century); standing today

where.modern_name: Ellora Caves, near Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad), Maharashtra, India
where.historical_name: Elapura (Verul Leni), under the Rashtrakuta dynasty at its height

importance.justification: A World Heritage site where Buddhist, Hindu and Jain temples sit side by side; the ASI calls the Kailasa the largest single monolithic excavation in the world.
